entry.title: Insolvency 36/2012: what the Court actually ordered
entry.summary: New primary-orders reader: the creditor-substitution order is body-dated 8 February 2018 and provides a twenty-day appeal; the 4 June clarification is complete at three pages; Order 164/2021 definitively approved CAM on 18 May after the third-party bidder's nonappearance and failure to lodge the bond; and the two 26 January 2022 orders are clarifications. The reader separates LPB estate property, third parties, premises, control, debt, deed, Registry, accounts and any surplus without inferring invalidity or nonpayment from a documentary absence.

entry.title: CEXP / Monterecco-Pink / Order 804: continuity and source access corrected
entry.summary: The 13 August forensic review and correction are recoverable through a public-safe continuity record and a private recovery checkpoint. CEXP retains the strongest located collective provenance without proved exclusivity; the 1 February 2012 notice, real 159-unit/477-bed operation and authority/scope gaps are confronted. Order 804/2018 remains an appellate affirmation of provisional criminal dismissal and adverse evidence, not a title trial or proof of total abandonment. Drive links are custody locators whose anonymous access has not been verified. Cabildo/RGT/Yaiza remain bounded document requests without a predetermined conclusion.

entry.title: JDAM / architecture / COALZ–COAGC: the visado as a documentary node in a wider chain
entry.summary: New bilingual source-controlled record: the 25 February 2022 visado is analysed as a possible documentary node between apparent authority, commission, project, Yaiza, tourism, investment, finance, RIC/REF, public support, operation and judicial evidence. The page records COALZ entries 26/008230, 26/008474 and 26/008476 with their limits; the unresolved COAGC professional-data discrepancy; the contextual PwC–Grant Thornton–San Telmo/RICPE–RSM chronology; two Spanish visual indexes with express evidential boundaries; and the status of the 20 August communications. Registration, forwarding or distribution does not mean investigation, breach or merits decision.

entry.title: RICPE / MYND Yaiza: public question on Decree 224/2022, AEAT and Series F/G
entry.summary: New open documentary record: RICPE's audited 2023 accounts separate Series F — Hotel MYND Yaiza, €1,598,849.32 — from Series G — employment creation, €4,974,853.78. The public question is whether Decree 224/2022 and the AEAT binding report of 17 November 2022 covered F, G or both, whether an additional/amended act existed, and what expenditure, liabilities or prior financing justified Series F in the refurbishment/opening chronology. No finding of illegality is made: the page identifies who has competence, which record would answer, and the status of access requests.

entry.title: RICPE: filing corroborated by Ethical Channel and native platform email
entry.summary: Gil Marer, writing from San Cristóbal de La Laguna, submitted a formal communication through the RICPE Ethical Channel on 17 August 2026. Submission is corroborated by the final platform screen and a native platform email timestamped 17 August 2026, 22:51:17 UTC confirming the communication and assignment of a private follow-up code. The contemporaneous Gmail chain also preserves a digitally signed 22-page PDF, 447,975 bytes, SHA-256 b455075ceda7841471ef5f4ebfbb784ccd00357439aa8bf282e736fe4757832c, whose cryptographic signature validates. That signed PDF differs materially from the earlier 21-page V6 baseline; it is therefore preserved as a later signed object and strong candidate for the filed attachment, while exact byte identity with the channel attachment remains pending platform metadata or certificate evidence. Admission, investigation, conflict screening, preservation measures, Board treatment and merits are not yet established. Access credentials remain private.

entry.title: RICPE / Sun Park / Orion: governance, finance, ERDF, Portfolio and CNMV
entry.summary: The controlled record moves from a linear reading to a documented architecture of governance, knowledge, management and finance. José Acosta Matos sat on the RICPE board before the 2020 Sun Park investor communications; RICPE’s July-2021 record documents fragmented title and conditionality; RICPE founded Orion and the Issue Document describes a 17% RICPE convertible participating-finance channel; AGM is identified as strategic/asset manager and the related-person disclosure reconnects JDAM with FMMM, Shaila Cogolludo, Antonio Cogolludo and Pamalexsha/related interests already present in the Sun Park record. Portfolio confirmed an internal investigation, CNMV said filing 2024136159 would be processed as a consultation, and MYND’s permanent plaque expressly identifies ERDF. The specific asset/value trail from Sun Park/MYND/LPB/Matkator into Orion remains open.

entry.title: Three-level LAJ supervisory chain activated
entry.summary: The same corpus was registered with the Canary Islands High Court Government Secretariat, the Las Palmas Provincial Coordination Secretariat and the national Secretariat-General for preservation, identification and reconstruction of the LAJ documentary chain. Registration does not mean that an investigation has opened.

entry.title: RICPE correction: Aweswell procedural representation and good-faith third-party exposure
entry.summary: The 26 May 2020 record establishes the change in Aweswell’s procedural representation in Concurso 36/2012, not a global termination. Any later effect on residual trust, confidentiality or assistance remains subject to proof.

entry.title: Lender of Record: credit chain and LPB concurso perimeter
entry.summary: The page separates the mortgage-credit chain from the disputed financial package and maintains that the limited LPB concurso is not automatic authority over the whole hotel, CEXP, Matkator/third parties, finance or later operation.
